audits.claim_text: The 84 by 133 score matrix is approximately rank 2: scores hidden from the matrix are best recovered using two factors.
audits.scope: May 2026 BenchPress matrix (84 models, 133 benchmarks, 2,604 cells). Soft-Impute hard-rank sweep in raw and logit space, held-out MedAPE on random per-model folds, plus a block holdout of the newest 17 models. Rank of the Bias ALS predictor is not swept.

run_selection.selection_rule: No runs were executed or selected. The audit reads every table, caption and passage in the paper that bears on the claim, including appendix material that weakens it.

check_results.rationale: Rank is chosen on held-out cells, and the appendix repeats the sweep with the newest 20 percent of models removed as a block and 95 percent cluster-bootstrap intervals over 17 models (appendix lines 497 to 508).
Held-out MedAPE is a reasonable criterion for predictive rank. It measures which hard rank predicts best under Soft-Impute, which is narrower than the dimension of the data-generating structure.

Only Soft-Impute is swept over rank. Under nested validation NMF selects rank 1 for all seven transforms and PMF selects rank 3 or 5 (appendix lines 787 to 830). The adopted Bias ALS has its rank fixed at 2 and carries a model offset in addition, so its fitted matrix has rank up to 4 in transformed space.

The main rank figure reports no uncertainty and the text gives no numeric values for ranks 1 and 3. In raw space under block holdout, ranks 2 and 3 are within each others interval and the curve is described as flat over the first three ranks.
Whether the rank-2 minimum in logit space is separated from rank 1 and rank 3 beyond the bootstrap interval is not stated in text; figures were not rendered for this audit.

Column standardisation and zero or mean initialisation interact with hard-rank truncation at 23.3 percent fill; an optimum at low rank can reflect regularisation need under sparsity as much as intrinsic dimension. Missingness is structured and held-out cells are drawn only from observed cells.
Every number audited is traceable to a table, caption or sentence in the v2 LaTeX source, and the source names the generating script for each table in comments. Nothing was rerun.
Standalone review of published text; no run snapshots or bindings exist to compare.
Single reviewer reading the authors own reported tables; no separate evaluation or advancement authority.

independence.evidence: The auditor is not an author of the paper but has no independent data or rerun.

limitations: The claim that survives is operational: with this matrix and Soft-Impute, hard rank 2 gives the lowest held-out MedAPE, and the logit-space minimum persists under a block holdout.
The abstract phrase that a models scores are largely determined by just two numbers is stronger than this. The adopted predictor uses three numbers per model (an offset and two factor scores).
Selected rank differs by method (NMF 1, PMF 3 or 5), so rank 2 is a property of the estimator and sparsity level as well as of the data.
The authors state the rank-2 geometry is a property of the current snapshot.

An exploratory in-house rerun by a separate workstream (one hide-half split, model-bootstrap intervals, version families not collapsed) sweeps the Bias ALS rank on the May matrix: rank 2 improves on rank 1 by 0.53 MedAE points [0.27, 0.70] and rank 3 adds 0.05 with an interval of [-0.27, 0.13]. Its absolute errors are higher than the papers, so it bears on the ordering of ranks only.

corrective_action.note: Sweep rank 0 to 4 for the Bias ALS predictor itself with intervals, and report the rank-1 and rank-3 held-out errors numerically.

audits.claim_text: BenchPress, a logit-space rank-2 matrix completion method, recovers held-out scores to within 4.6 points.
audits.scope: May 2026 matrix; random per-model holdout of observed cells, 10 seeds by 3 folds; median absolute error in raw score points at 100 percent coverage; default Logit Bias ALS, rank 2, lambda 0.1.

run_selection.selection_rule: No runs were executed or selected. The audit reads every table, caption and passage in the paper that bears on the claim, including appendix material that weakens it.

check_results.rationale: Held-out folds take no part in hyperparameter selection; selection uses nested validation cells, and the nested ranking also places the default first (appendix line 706).
MedAE is defined and computed consistently. It is a median: half of held-out cells miss by more than 4.63 points. The abstract wording within 4.6 points omits the word median.
84 transform-method pairs are tuned the same way on the same folds. Reference points on the same protocol: benchmark mean 10.04, model mean 7.22, logit Soft-Impute 5.10, identity Bias ALS 5.17.

The hide fraction is ambiguous (half, one third, or about 26 percent implied by the stated 20,000 test predictions over 30 folds). Regression methods with lower MedAPE are set aside for incomplete coverage, which is disclosed.
No interval on 4.63. The top full-coverage configurations differ by 0.01 points. The papers own conformal intervals for this predictor are 19.56 points wide at 80 percent and 27.01 at 90 percent.

Held-out cells are a random subset of observed cells, so the error describes cells that someone chose to run and report. The 76.7 percent of cells never observed are not represented, and the authors state missingness is structured. Vendor-reported best-configuration scores dominate the matrix.

audits.claim_text: PKPS matches the accuracy of the sample score with up to an 8 times smaller query budget.
audits.scope: HELM-Lite suite (18 tasks, 93 models) and EEE suite (16 tasks, 45 models), dense matrices with sparsity induced by uniform masking; unpaired per-model query pools; leave-one-family-out K-NN; MAE on a 0 to 1 scale over 16 seeds.

run_selection.selection_rule: No runs were executed or selected. The audit reads every table, caption and passage in the paper that bears on the claim, including appendix material that weakens it.

check_results.rationale: Targets are full-depth task means that are never embedded; the regressor excludes the target developers models; bandwidth and ensemble weights are chosen on observed scores of other families.
MAE against the true full-task score is the natural metric. Tasks with 42 and 1,319 items get equal weight.

IRT is fit on the largest fully observed block and is poorly identified by design under unpaired pools, as the authors note, so it is a weak baseline here. DKPS is disadvantaged by the unpaired design that the experiment constructs. The sample score is the meaningful comparator.
Table 1 reports both suites and both budgets, including cells where PKPS alone is not best (HELM at 8 queries: sample 0.092, PKPS 0.109).

Wilcoxon over per-task differences, ensemble against sample score at one query: p of 8e-6 on HELM, better on all 18 tasks. SEM over 16 seeds. No multiplicity correction is stated and tasks within a dataset are not independent.

Sparsity is uniform masking of models that ran everything; the paper names non-uniform observation as an open limitation. The embedding is transductive (the target is embedded jointly). Only one embedding model is tested.

audits.claim_text: Benchmark prediction using PKPS is query-efficient relative to methods that only use information from dense and paired portions of the evaluation data (Theorem 2), and the experiments are its empirical counterpart.
audits.scope: Theorems 1 and 2 and their proofs in Appendix D, read against the estimator actually run in Section 4.

run_selection.selection_rule: No runs were executed or selected. The audit reads every table, caption and passage in the paper that bears on the claim, including appendix material that weakens it.

check_results.rationale: The proofs were read and no error was found, but they were not formally checked. The estimator in Theorem 2 (three-way split, Nystrom extension, guarded bandwidth selection with a 2 tau margin, exact reference scores) is not the estimator in the experiments (joint embedding, leave-one-model-out K-NN bandwidth choice, no guard, sample scores as targets).
Mean squared error dominance at a fixed budget is a clear criterion; the definition allows equality except at one n.

Part (i) holds for any estimator family that contains the comparator and selects with a guard, so it does not rest on PKPS geometry. Part (ii) compares against DKPS in the case where DKPS has no shared queries and can only predict the mean.
Assumptions 1 to 7 are stated explicitly, including uniform subsampling and i.i.d. models and caches.
The Theorem 1 bound grows linearly in the number of models and as the inverse square of the cross-model kernel mass, and is not evaluated numerically on either suite.
Uniform observation and i.i.d. models are assumed; the synthetic overlap sweep (Figure 2 panel b) is the only direct empirical counterpart.
